summary: This program builds a list of Song objects and then sorts the same list three times — by title, by energy level from high to low, and by artist — using the List.sort method with different Comparator objects.

lines.text: Comparator lives in java.util and supplies the factory methods used below to describe sort orders.
The variable is declared as the List interface but holds an ArrayList, so the code depends only on the general list behaviour.
Each add call appends one Song to the end of the list, so the starting order is the order the songs were added.
An enhanced for loop walks the list once to show the unsorted order before any sorting happens.
Comparator.comparing builds a comparator that compares songs by whatever getTitle returns, and sort rearranges the list in place using it.
The forEach method is a compact alternative to writing a loop, and System.out::println is a method reference telling it to print each element.
comparingInt is the version for int values, which avoids wrapping each energy level in an Integer object.
Calling reversed on a comparator flips its order, turning the low-to-high energy sort into high-to-low.
Because sort reorders the list itself rather than returning a copy, this third sort starts from whatever order the previous sort left behind.
